core_obligations: Apply the pointwise variant at the points of the fibre: for each x in X_s find an elementary etale neighbourhood of the base and an etale neighbourhood Y_x of x over the base change, affine, with the pulled back module having free global sections and preserved residue fields, so that the image of the fibre of Y_x is an open neighbourhood of x in the fibre (proof lines 3651-3669).

Pass to finitely many points and dominate: since the fibre is quasi-compact, cover it by finitely many of those neighbourhoods and choose one elementary etale neighbourhood of the base dominating all of them (proof lines 3670-3676).

Assemble the global neighbourhood: take X' to be the disjoint union of the base changed pieces with the obvious morphism to X, so that the fibre is covered by its image and the global sections of the pulled back module are the direct sum of the base changes of the pointwise free modules, hence free over the new base (proof lines 3677-3692).
proof_roadmap: Cover the fibre using the pointwise variant (proof lines 3651-3669).
Choose a single dominating elementary etale neighbourhood (proof lines 3670-3676).
Take the disjoint union and compute its global sections (proof lines 3677-3692).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the finite type (as opposed to finite presentation) form of the freeness statement along a fibre: after an elementary etale neighbourhood of the point of the base there is an affine etale neighbourhood of the fibre on which the pulled back finite type module has free global sections (statement lines 3626-3649, tag 05L1). The proof is the same assembling argument as in the finite presentation case: apply the pointwise variant at the points of the quasi-compact fibre, pass to finitely many points, choose one dominating elementary etale neighbourhood, and then take the disjoint union of the base changed pieces, whose global sections are a direct sum of base changes of free modules. The assembling step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
